2:internalId: a073f9b2-b7e9-42c1-9449-a8fb10c6a04e
74:- Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing.
75:- Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file.
76:- **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it.
80:- `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`.
82:- A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment.
152:- Cards have potentially stable `header.internalId` and user-facing `header.id`.

`ProjectCard`, `ProjectSnapshot`, `MarkdownFile`, and the bridge contracts are defined in [data_types.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/data/data_types.ts:46). Electron returns markdown files; React creates `ProjectCard` objects in [markdown_parsing_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/markdown_parsing_service.ts:353).

Electron retains some transient stateâ€”current project, running executions, locks, schedules, watchersâ€”but not the rendererâ€™s complete card snapshot.

## Cards versus regular markdown files

A project folder contains both cards and ordinary markdown documents. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content:

- Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing.
- Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file.
- **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it.

Consequences:

- `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`.
- Regular markdown files are identified by path alone, everywhere.
- A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment.

The classification is applied in [markdown_parsing_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/markdown_parsing_service.ts:355).

entries.content:
The cause is in card classification and ID migration. The project loader reads Markdown throughout the project folder, and the watcher reloads changes there. Those files become `backgroundCards`. The ID migration then adds an `internalId` to **every Markdown file under the configured releases or archive folder** that lacks one, without checking whether it is a card. That makes `release_notes.md` eligible. See [project_loading.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts:1029), [project_state.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_state.ts:389), and [card_internal_id_operations.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/card_internal_id_operations.ts:13).

This can happen on the full project load as well as after a watcher event. The existing test explicitly expects missing IDs to be added to files in the archive and releases folders, so it also encodes the overly broad rule: [card_operations.test.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/card_operations.test.ts:160). The rule conflicts with the documented model, which says a file in those folders **without** an ID is ordinary Markdown: [current_data_model.md](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/architecture/current_data_model.md:72).

On the release notes question: all 11 `design/releases/**/release_notes.md` files currently have IDs. I found no release note specific code that reads those IDs or a reference to the sampled IDs elsewhere. The app does load the notes through its generic background card model, so the IDs can participate in generic card behavior. The release process identifies the notes by their **path**; archived release cards do need IDs for card activity handling. I would not treat the notes’ existing IDs as evidence that release publishing needs them.

This was a read-only investigation; I changed no files and ran no tests.
